title: Retroactive vs. Prospective Examination Finding Under Superseded Regulation
scenario_text:
During Cascade Financial Group's 2025 safety and soundness examination, an OCC examiner issued a Matter Requiring Attention (MRA) referencing BSA/AML transaction monitoring thresholds. The finding creates a temporal consistency puzzle across multiple systems.

**Archer GRC — Examination Finding EF-2025-007 (Filed April 22, 2025)**
Type: MRA | Examiner: OCC Field Office, Charlotte
Finding: "The institution's automated transaction monitoring system failed to generate alerts for structuring patterns below the $3,000 threshold during the review period (July 2024 — December 2024)."
Regulation cited: 12 CFR 1010.320 (as amended, effective March 1, 2024)
Remediation deadline: August 31, 2025

**SharePoint — /policies/bsa-aml/monitoring-thresholds (Page version 8, published January 2025)**
Section 2.1: "Automated monitoring shall flag potential structuring activity at thresholds of $3,000 and above, per revised regulatory guidance effective March 2024."
[Version 5 (published February 2024) stated: "...thresholds of $5,000 and above, consistent with long-standing FinCEN guidance..."]
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @d.kapoor, Feb 28, 2024]: "Legal confirmed: the March 1 effective date applies prospectively. We don't need to re-run historical transactions. Just update the threshold going forward."

**ServiceNow — CHG-2024-1847 (System change request)**
Requester: D. Kapoor | Submitted: Feb 15, 2024 | Approved: Feb 27, 2024
Change: Update AML monitoring threshold from $5,000 to $3,000
Implementation date: March 4, 2024 (3 days after regulatory effective date)
CAB notes: "Approved for March 4 deployment window. 3-day gap between effective date and implementation is within acceptable tolerance per vendor SLA."

**Microsoft Teams — #bsa-compliance (April 24, 2025, 9:15 AM)**
@robert.nakamura: Has anyone reviewed the EF-2025-007 finding closely? The review period starts July 2024 but I want to confirm our system was running at $3K by then.
@deepa.kapoor: We went live March 4. So July onwards was definitely at the $3K threshold.
@robert.nakamura: Then why the finding? Were there gaps in coverage?
@deepa.kapoor: Let me check with the vendor. Could be a model tuning issue vs. a threshold issue.
@robert.nakamura: 🤔
[No further replies]

**Outlook — Subject: "Confidential: AML vendor call notes" (April 28, 2025)**
From: d.kapoor@cascadefinancial.com
To: r.nakamura@cascadefinancial.com

Robert — just got off the call with FIS. Here's the issue: when we updated the threshold in March 2024, the change applied to NEW transaction monitoring rules only. The legacy Piedmont Bank rules (migrated during the 2022 acquisition) were running on a separate rule engine instance. Those rules were still at $5K until the December 2024 platform consolidation. So any Piedmont-originated accounts with structuring patterns between $3K-$5K from March through November 2024 would not have alerted.

This only affects ~400 accounts in the legacy Piedmont segment. I haven't told the exam team yet. What's our exposure here?
question: What is Cascade Financial Group's strongest defensible position when responding to the MRA regarding the March-November 2024 monitoring gap on legacy Piedmont accounts?

contributor.name: Robert Nakamura
contributor.title: Regulatory Change Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Regulatory implementation, policy versioning, transition periods, grandfathering provisions, compliance attestation

choices: The finding should be challenged — Cascade's internal policy (SharePoint v5) was at $5,000 until the update, and the resolved comment confirms legal advised the new threshold applies prospectively only, meaning historical Piedmont transactions need not be re-monitored

The finding is time-barred — the examination review period begins July 2024, but the monitoring gap started March 2024, and the OCC should have identified this in the prior examination cycle; Cascade can argue lack of timely supervisory notice as a mitigating factor

The gap is a de minimis technical issue — the regulation took effect March 1 but Cascade's policy correctly set the $3,000 threshold and the 3-day implementation delay was within acceptable tolerance; the legacy engine issue is a vendor defect, not a compliance failure

The gap represents a genuine compliance deficiency — the regulation was effective March 1, 2024, Cascade's policy was updated to reflect the $3,000 threshold, but implementation was incomplete because the legacy Piedmont rule engine was not included in the system change; the institution's control environment failed to ensure the policy was operationalized across all platforms
